notes: Closed after the fact. The work landed in PR #290 without a closing keyword in the PR body, so GitHub never closed #293 itself and the issue sat open over landed code - the same silence the receipt-preservation guard was built for, one level up. Recorded so the ledger says why the close is late rather than pretending it was timely. GATE HISTORY, recorded rather than hidden: this receipt was refused twice. First for putting the LANDED head in currentHead, which is the head a transition is authorized FROM, not the head work landed at. Then for citing a gate run and a review bound to that landed head - 'a review of earlier code does not cover the commits after it'. Both refusals were correct, and neither was worked around. The lesson is the one the ledger already teaches elsewhere: close the issue from the lane that landed it, while still standing on the proven head. A close done later has to earn proof at the head it is done from.
